questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Sydney as my study destination because it offers the chance to live in a vibrant international city with stunning nature nearby and an amazing lifestyle. The University of Sydney's strong reputation for high-quality education was also a major factor, along with the opportunity to improve my English in an English-speaking environment.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy to find the information I needed upon arrival. The university provided clear pre-arrival guides, and there were plenty of online resources outlining practical details like transportation, accommodation, and campus orientation.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When I arrived, I received assistance through the university's orientation program, which included campus tours, informational sessions, and social events for international students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are several options for student accommodation on campus, with varying prices and facilities. Some offer private studios with a kitchen and bathroom, while others provide single rooms with shared kitchen and bathroom facilities. I'm familiar with Scape, Abercrombie Student Accommodation, and Queen Mary Building.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In the Queen Mary Building, there was a communal kitchen on the ground floor equipped with all amenities, including extra space to store food in the fridge. Each floor also had a kitchenette with a microwave, and every room featured a spacious fridge and integrated freezer. Additionally, the university had a variety of food stalls, and during the exam period, many meals were provided for free, which I found very thoughtful.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: On-campus housing provides a great and comfortable start to your university life, offering a solid foundation for your studies and an excellent opportunity to meet other students. While it's conveniently close to the university, it is somewhat farther from the city center. Rent in Sydney can be high, and availability is limited, but if you're up for the challenge, I would recommend finding your own place closer to the beaches or in a local neighborhood to fully experience everything Sydney has to offer.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process at the University of Sydney was smooth and well-supported. I had a student counsellor from the university who was very informative and provided clear guidance throughout. They helped me with all the necessary steps, from course selection to understanding the requirements for registration.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always email the student counsellor for assistance, but the university's website was also a valuable resource, providing detailed information. Additionally, a Google Sheet with helpful links about the courses and other relevant resources was shared, making it easy to find everything you needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I found it very easy to register for the classes I wanted. The process was straightforward, and I was able to select my desired courses without any issues.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My advice to future exchange students would be to remember to thoroughly read the emails you receive from the student counsellor at the host university. All the information you need for registration and other important steps is included in those emails, and by doing so, you won't miss any deadlines. If you have a question, make sure to check the emails first before reaching out to the student counsellor.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was appropriate for all the ones I took. Some courses were more challenging than others and required more time, especially because some of the content was completely new. On the other hand, some courses involved repetition of material I had already learned, which was then built upon.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The mix of lectures and tutorials was similar to what I'm used to. There was a lot of group work in the courses I chose, just like at UCPH, which I found to be a great way to meet new people from different cultures while also strengthening my collaboration skills. However, I noticed there was a greater focus on attendance, tests, and grades, which were aspects I had to adjust to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would highly recommend the courses Responsible Design for Innovation and Digital Business Innovation, as they offer insights into the intersections of communication, technology, and innovation. These courses provide valuable perspectives on how responsible design and digital innovation are shaping industries and influencing the future of business. Additionally, if you have an interest in marketing, Marketing Principles is an excellent choice. The course covers foundational marketing concepts in an engaging way, offering both theoretical and practical applications.  

All of these courses are supported by passionate teaching teams, making the learning experience very enjoyable!

questions.answer: Groceries are a bit more expensive, but other than that, the prices are similar to those in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were plenty of opportunities to join a club. At the beginning of the semester, they held two days with stalls where you could ask questions and learn more. There was a wide variety of societies to choose from, such as the Surfing Society, Chocolate Society, Bushwalkers, and many more. I highly recommend joining a club to meet new friends and have a break from studying all the time.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Whatever sparks your interest or if you're looking to try something new. There are plenty of athletic facilities on campus, including tennis courts, a gym, and a swimming pool. It's a great way to have fun and stay active.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Australia has so much to offer! In Sydney, make sure to check out its amazing beaches and explore the city itself. You could also take a van trip along the East Coast to visit Byron Bay and try surfing, or head north to Cairns to experience the Great Barrier Reef and the beautiful Whitsundays. For a truly unique adventure, don't miss the opportunity to visit the iconic Uluru in the Outback.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. I didn't encounter any issues along the way.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be persistent! If making friends with local students is a goal for you, keep pursuing it. Once you get to know them, they are the nicest people, but there might be a bit of a shell to get past at first.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: To be honest, there weren't many cultural differences in Australia. However, there are a lot of international students at Australian universities pursuing their full education. Sometimes, it could be a bit challenging to communicate due to a language barrier, but I wouldn't say it was a major issue.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated the openness and kindness of the people in Australia. The locals are generally warm and welcoming, which made it easy to feel comfortable and build connections. I also loved the easygoing lifestyle outside of the university. People seem to prioritize a good work-life balance, with plenty of time for outdoor activities, socializing, and enjoying nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Be prepared for a more performance-driven academic environment. 
The academic culture in Australia might have a stronger focus on attendance, participation, and grades compared to what you might be used to at UCPH. Stay on top of deadlines, and be ready to engage in more frequent assessments such as quizzes or participation points.

2) Explore beyond the city. 
Australia offers so much more than just city life. Take the time to travel around and experience different parts of the country.

3) Don't hesitate to ask for help. 
If you're unsure about anything, whether it's academic or personal, the support services are there for you. Whether it's the student counselor, professors, or fellow students, don't be afraid to ask questions. The academic system might be different, and getting advice early can save you time and stress.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I recommend reading through these travel reports, as I found them very helpful before my exchange. They offer useful information not only about your host institution but also about other destinations in Australia, helping you prepare for what to expect.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was meeting such kind people from all over the world and connecting with locals, even though they had busy schedules and jobs. I met the locals through my courses, where we had the opportunity to be creative in our work. This not only allowed me to collaborate with others but also gave me many fresh new perspectives that I truly appreciated.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during my exchange was juggling having fun and studying at the same time. My schedule was quite tight from Monday to Wednesday, which made it difficult to balance academic commitments with exploring and enjoying my time in the city. You want to do everything and make the most out of your exchange while you're there, but it's really important to prioritize and choose between things.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
